To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intrinsic motivation and independent learning expectations are better predictors of withdrawal from higher education than extrinsic motivation and lack of direction, although gender and faculty of education have an effect.
intrinsic motivation and independent expectations were the most useful predictors of HE withdrawal.
the strongest predictor of first year HE withdrawal is intrinsic motivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model to explain and predict withdrawal from HE.
identifying the predictors of withdrawal from higher education and, more specifically, the relative contribution of demographic and psychological variables to withdrawal.
the development of a model of HE withdrawal, and the identification of factors that predict withdrawal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best predictor of withdrawal is the student's past academic performance.

, while the prediction of withdrawal is not a simple matter, it is possible to identify some factors that are related to continuance and withdrawal, and that these factors are amenable to interventions.
the prediction of HE withdrawal is not yet possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HE institutions should be concerned about students with low intrinsic motivation, low expectations of independent study and low performance.
the most useful predictor of HE withdrawal is the student's own perception of the likelihood of success.
the best way of predicting withdrawal from HE would be to wait until students are enrolled in HE courses and then to monitor their performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best predictors of withdrawal from higher education are those that are most proximal to the actual experience of higher education.
it is possible to identify students at risk for withdrawal, and to intervene to improve the likelihood of their success in higher education.
the prediction of HE withdrawal can be improved by the inclusion of more measures of students’ academic self-efficacy and their motivation.
